Press Release:


Pressure on Pravin
In February this year, just before Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan delivered a highly anticipated budget speech, news broke that he was being investigated by the Hawks in relation to an intelligence unit within the SA Revenue Service established in 2007—during his tenure as Commissioner there. In August Gordhan declined to appear before the Hawks as requested. Then, on Tuesday—two weeks before delivery of his medium term budget—the NPA announced that a summons, on charges of alleged fraud, had been delivered to him. Support for Gordhan has poured in from various quarters and, while the Minister has spent much time reassuring investors that the economy is making a turnaround, every move against him has sent shock waves through the markets and hit the rand hard, renewing fears of a downgrade to junk status. Carte Blanche brings key analysis to these developments.


Script:


PRAVIN PRESSURED

PRODUCER: ESTÉ DE KLERK

PRESENTER: DEREK WATTS

EDITOR: STENETTE GROSSKOPF

BROADCAST DATE: 16 OCTOBER 2016

DEREK LINK: It’s a tale of a political triangle and alleged inteference, questionable timing and unclear motives - with the Finance Minister and SARS up against the Hawks and the NPA. Somewhere in between is President Jacob Zuma. A slimy web of politics is playing itself out.

Since allegations against Finance Minister, Pravin Ghordhan started to surface early this year, very few questions have actually been answered with facts.

AUBREY MATSHIQI: To me this is in all probablity a battle between devils with halos and angels with horns.

And this, says political analyst, Aubrey Matseqi, points to internal power struggles amongst members of the state and the ruling party.

AUBREY MATSHIQI: There is an allegation that Pravin Gordhan is a victim of a political conspiracy, because acting in the interests of Jacob Zuma or at his behest are those trying to capture National Treasury, because National treasury is a hindrance when it comes to looting state resources.

At a press conference on Tuesday, NPA head, advocate Shaun Abrahams announced that Minister Gordhan, together with former SARS Commissioner, Oupa Magashula and former deputy SARS Commissioner, Ivan Pillay would be prosecuted and charged with fraud, or alternatively with theft.

ADV. SHAUN ABRAHAMS: In respect of the R1 141 178.11 whereby the aforementioned persons had misrepresented to the Government Employment Pension Fund and to SARS.

In 2009, Pillay applied for early retirement to obtain his pension pay-out. He also requested to be re-appointed on a contract basis in a different capacity.
The request was made to Magashula, SARS Commissioner at the time, who in turn had to get approval from then Finance Minister, Pravin Gordhan.
Pillay received his pension with full benefits in 2010 and was then re-appointed.

ADV. SHAUN ABRAHAMS: the employee-initiated severance package was not applicable to Mr Pillay.

According to Advocate Abrahams, certain rules of the Government Employment Pension Fund were not adhered to.
Magashula and Pillay will also be charged with contravening the Public Finance Management Act for irregular expenditure; as well as another fraud charge.

ADV. SHAUN ABRAHAMS: Mr Pillay also entered into a 5 year contract with SARS as the Deputy Commissioner instead of on a three year contract and instead of in a different capacity.

Minister Gordhan and Pillay will further be charged with another count of fraud in relation to the extention of the contract.

PROF. MCEBISI NDLETYANA: I was surprised by the nature of the charge. We have always known that Zuma did not want Gordhan.

UJ Political Science associate professor, Mkabisi Ndlatyana says it’s possible that the Finance Minister is seen as an inconvenience to some factions in government.

PROF. MCEBISI NDLETYANA: The presidency has been captured. The executive authority does not rest with presidency. It rests elsewhere with his handler and patrons.

Economist, dr Iraj Abedian says the credibility of the NPA and Hakws is on the line.

DR IRAJ ABEDIAN: This case got to do with early retirement of deputy commissioner. This is not organized crime.

Minister Ghordhan and his Treasury team has miraculously steadied the economy since December when Moody’s downgraded our rating from stable to negative. This happened after President Zuma fired Finance Minister, Nhlanhla Nene; appointed Des van Rooyen for four days and then re-appointed Minister Gordhan.

DR IRAJ ABEDIAN: He fought hard and deep with the rating agencies to defend our investment rate.

Minister Gordhan was at a Gauteng Tender Summit when the news broke.
In a statement he said that the “nature of the charges against him was difficult for him to appreciate”.

PRAVIN GORDHAN: South Africans should really ask themselves who are the Hawks or these few people in the Hawks really serving? Where are they getting their political instructions from and for what purpose?

DEREK LINK: The Hawks have been circling since February this year when he was asked to answer the now infamous 27 questions in an investigation into the so-called sars rogue unit while the minister was the sars commissioner. in may, he was told he was no suspect. and in august, on legal advise, minister gordhan declined to present himself to the Hawks for a warning statement.

The warning statement related to Pillay’s early retirement, as well as the controversial SARS unit – established in 2007 to probe tax defaulters. This unit would later be accused of going rogue, allegations that have never been proven.
Although the Hawks’ investigation is not yet concluded, advocate Abrahams said the establishment of the unit was in conflict with the Constitution and SARS legislation.
Minister Gordhan has maintained throughout that the unit was lawfully founded and he was unaware of any rogue activities.

DEREK LINK: PRESIDENT ZUMA HAS REAFFIRMED HIS SUPPORT FOR MINISTER GORDHAN AND ADDED THAT THE NPA’S DECISION CAME AT THE MOST SENSITIVE TIME FOR THE COUNTRY.

A sensitive time, the President said, because Minister Gordhan “was successfully leading initiatives towards economic revival... to reignite growth”.

DEREK LINK: BUT, IS THE PRESIDENT JUST PLAYING A CLEVER GAME OF POKER?

AUBREY MATSHIQI: At the slightest of provocations the president will remind us that Des Van Rooyen was the best candidate for FM ever since 1994.


The Finance Ministry says it’s quite clear that “these proceedings are contaminated by abuse for political ends”.

ADV. SHAUN ABRAHAM: I can assue you there has been no political interference in this matter.

A day after the shock announcement, advocate Abrahams backtracked when he faced Parliament’s Justice Committee, saying he was willing to review the decision to prosecute the Minister if approached to do so.
In a terse statement on Friday, Minister Gordhan said he will not be making representations to advocate Abrahams, adding that he doesn’t have any confidence in advocate Abrahams’s ability to afford him a fair hearing.

PROF. MCEBISI NDLETYANA: No one has ever as far as I know, no one has ever been charged with one irregular expenditure and extending someone’s contract. These two things happen in public service all the time.

DEREK LINK: TIMING, THEY SAY, IS EVERYTHING AND SOME SEE A SINISTER LINK BETWEEN THE NPA ANNOUNCEMNET AND GORDHAN’S MID-TERM BUDGET SPEECH AND THE PUBLIC PROTECTOR’S REPORT ON STATE CAPTURE.

Outgoing Public Protector, advocate Thuli Madonsela didn’t release her much anticipated State Capture report on Friday. The President and Co-operative Governance Minister, Des van Rooyen have both applied for urgent court applications to halt her.

MCEBISI NDLETYANA: Treasury has been working with Madonsela’s office giving her all in information.

AUBREY MATSHIQI: Timing should never be an issue. It Arises because of perception that the NPA and Hawks are tools that are being used in this alleged conspiracy against the Finance Minister.

On Wednesday, the Supreme Court of Appeal granted President Zuma a temporary lifeline by allowing his legal team an opportunity to argue why he should be permitted to appeal the so-called spy tapes judgment. Earlier this year, the Pretoria High Court ruled that the 2009 decision to withdraw fraud and corruption charges against the President was “irrational” and set aside.

DEREK LINK: BUT HOW WILL THE MAJORITY OF OUR POPULATION BE AFFECTED BY THIS LATEST CHAPTER IN A LONG-RUNNING SAGA?

Within the hour following the NPA’s announcement, the rand plummeted by 3,4% to the US Dollar.

DR IRAJ ABEDIAN: We get downgraded not just to junk but two or three degrees, which will then condemn the country’s growth for the 30 years to a high cost of capital.

And it will ultimately be the man on the street who suffers the most.

DR IRAJ ABEDIAN: The picture looks very bleak. Look what happened to Greece, look what happened to Spain. Look what is happening to Mexico. the working class pays the highest fee .

Support for the Minister has poured in from all corners.
And even with this sword hanging over his head, Minister Gordhan said he intended “to continue doing his job and that the cause of defending ethical leadership in government is too important to be deterred by this kind of harassment”.

AUBREY MATSHIQI: what I am certain of is that doubts about the independence between NPA and hawks will persist. What I am in doubt of is that in every case that involves I am in battle the Hawks have not been independent. But that uncertainty is the price we pay today because of sins by leaders of ANC since June 2005 of using state institutions in pursuit of narrow political ends.



PROMOS

PROMO 1: 15”

AUBREY MATSIQI: this is in all probablity a battle between devils with halos and angels with horns.


A web of political intrigue is unraveling as the finance minister faces fraud charges.

PROMO 2:15”

AUBREY MATSIQI: There is an allegation that Pravin Gordhan is a victim of a political conspiracy.
The Finance Minister summonsed to appear in court on fraud charges renews fears of an economic downgrade to junk status.
PROMO 3:10”
As the finance minister is summonsed to appear in court on fraud charges, the South African economy is facing a downgrade to junk status. Are we heading for financial meltdown.
